Your care provider or health plan believes Medicare will probably not pay for your home health care after this date.
If you keep getting care after this date, you may have to pay for it yourself.
**You have the right to appeal**
- An outside doctor or expert will review your case right away. This person does not work for your provider or plan.
- Your care will keep going while the review is happening.
The reviewer will want to hear what you think.
You do not have to write anything down. You can if you want to.
- The reviewer will also look at your medical records and other facts about your case.
- After you ask for an appeal, you will get a letter. It will explain in detail why your care should end.
- If the reviewer agrees that Medicare should stop paying, then Medicare and your plan will not pay for care after March 14, 2025.
- If the reviewer agrees that Medicare should stop paying, then Medicare and your plan will not pay for care after March 14, 2025.
- If you stop your care by March 14, 2025, you will not owe money for it.

- Ask as soon as you can.
- The last time you can ask is **noon on Thursday, March 13, 2025**. That is the day before your coverage ends.
To ask, call the Quality Improvement Organization.
The QIO is a group that Medicare trusts to review these decisions.
If you miss the deadline, you may still be able to appeal.
If you miss the deadline, you may still be able to appeal.
- Your QIO is **Midsouth Quality Review**. Their phone number is **1-888-555-0142**. You can also call this number if you have questions.

- The QIO will tell you its decision as soon as it can. This is usually within two days after March 14, 2025.
